translations.text: That is: in general, he is God to everyone in the first creation. Otherwise, "to my God" in a special sense, because he has given him the Holy Spirit and the grace of preaching.
That is: he is God to me because I believe in Jesus Christ, as he himself said: "No one comes to the Father," etc.

That is: it is famous in every land that you have believed in God, and we gain much from it. Because the chief rulers of the world have believed, everyone will believe afterwards, and whoever believes will not fear persecution.
That is: he knows. Nothing is hidden from him.
So there are two possible readings here: "I make remembrance without ceasing," or "in my prayers without ceasing."
That is: to see whether [?] the journey.
That is: that I may come.
What brings me to you? That is not hard to say: "for I desire."
That is: he does not mean a complete giving, because they already had some of it before. He means whatever is still missing from the perfection of your faith, so that I may complete it.
That is: so that the perfection of faith in you may be a comfort to me, and that the perfection of your faith may belong to me.
and sisters
That is: indeed [?]
That is: until now.
That is, here: so that he may have the fruit of his ministry with God. The great number of people who believe through his preaching increases his reward.
That is: to all the wise Gentiles.
That is: to the foolish.
That is: I am bound to preach to everyone, because I speak in the tongues of all. So I am a debtor to all, wise and unwise.
That is: I am ready.
That is: I am not ashamed to preach the gospel, that is, to preach the passion and incarnation of Christ, because miracles follow it, that is, the resurrection and ascension and ... [?]
He says, "Go, teach all nations." So they come first by race, not first by faith [?].
That is: recognition and worship, because they cannot help serving.
That is: knowable. From his work it is clear to them that there is a true one who orders all things [?].
That is: the elements. Through them his eternity can be seen [?] ...orum [?]
That is: as he is God.
That is: they did not honour God.
Pelagius: "withdrawing from the light of truth", i.e. from the light of the knowledge of God.
i.e. it is not the form itself that they worshipped, but a likeness of the form [?] ... [?] ... [?] ...
i.e. so that they [?] their bodies [?] ...
Pelagius: "among themselves", i.e. while they inflict cauteries and burnings on themselves in the rites of idols. "Cauteries", i.e. cuttings.
Pelagius: "for the reasons mentioned", i.e. because it is the creature they have served, and not the Creator.
i.e. each with the other.
i.e. the shame.
i.e. it is to them that the wages of their sin are paid.
i.e. in every unrighteousness.
i.e. whisperers, i.e. people who speak not to someone's face but into the ear.
i.e. slander [?].
i.e. they are deserving, or they are [?].
i.e. O every man, i.e. O each man.
i.e. by will, i.e. by consent.

"the evil which another does", i.e. you who consent to the one doing it. It is not that it would be wrong to rebuke others, but it is not enough for righteousness if you are evil and rebuke evil, i.e. it is judged, i.e. if it is reproved; and when he does this afterwards [?] that person, "you condemn yourself", i.e. it is clear that you are a wicked person, since the evil to which you consent is judged and reproved.
i.e. vengeance.
i.e. it will not be a help to him, but it will be left to a just judge.
i.e. [?] or a question.
i.e. goodness.
i.e. to draw your mind to repentance, he gives you every good thing.
i.e. that one.

i.e. Pelagius: because the saints will shine like the sun. Let us not think, then, that the glory is the same: "Come", etc. Honour: "possess", or the honour of the sons of God, through which they will judge the fugitive angels.
i.e. enduring every tribulation in the present while striving for glory and honour in the future.
i.e. a beating, i.e. every injury.
i.e. the more (so).
i.e. it is not persons that he regards, but works; i.e. it will not protect them, though they say, 'The law has not come to us.'
i.e. just as there was no moderation in the sin, there will be no moderation in the punishment.
i.e. a punishment according to law upon them.
i.e. the law which they have transgressed, it is through it that they will die.
i.e. a bond.
i.e. their conscience is a witness to them.
i.e. their thoughts consider what good it would be to do, and they strengthen the doing of that good; but they reprove the evil deed and forbid it.
i.e. the secret will not be good: the hidden things of men on that day.
i.e. it is through Jesus that I preach; or: God the Father will judge through Jesus Christ, i.e. it is the Son who will judge on the day of judgement, since he has given all judgement to the Son.
i.e. you do not trust in anything else.
you teach [?]
i.e. denial of God.
i.e. he is despised.

Pelagius: You call yourself blessed because you know God's will, but while you pass over the sense of the law, which concerns the incarnation of Christ, you dishonour God; or: in that you do not believe in Christ, whom the law preaches.
i.e. circumcision protects, [?] of the law; for in their view the one who was not circumcised was liable to death.
i.e. the mysteries of the law, as the law prophesied Christ.
i.e. it is the same as if he were not circumcised.
i.e. uncircumcision.
i.e. whoever has the righteousness of the law.
i.e. it is the same for him as if he were circumcised.
i.e. he will judge [?] you, O Jew, i.e. he will be better than you are.
i.e. before everyone.
i.e. O Jews, i.e. the circumcision that everyone sees does not profit you.
i.e. if that is so, what more is there in circumcision? 'What is the profit' etc. So it is not the profit of circumcision that he is dealing with, but it is a praise of the Jews.
'Much', i.e. it is in many ways that the Jew is better than the Gentile. This is an answer on behalf of the Jew to the Gentile.
i.e. does he set [them] before [others]? i.e. 'praeponit' (he puts before)
i.e. our sins
i.e. so that he is the more righteous because of it
i.e. for this evil
if the truth of God is the greater because of it
i.e. beforehand
i.e. why then am I made a sinner?
i.e. 'not as we are reproached', i.e. it is likely that it is not so
i.e. as they say
to say, i.e. that we say, i.e. they accuse us of saying it, as Paul said: 'where sin abounded, grace abounded the more', etc.
i.e. none of us surpasses another; all are guilty
i.e. against all the Gentiles
i.e. we have put [?] everyone's case (literally 'foot' [?]); no one is better than another in it
i.e. being without knowledge causes unrighteousness
i.e. because they did not serve, that caused them to be without knowledge and without righteousness
i.e. because they did not serve God
i.e. without exception
even as far as the one, or until the one, i.e. until Christ, for he found no good before him in the world
i.e. with every kind of bitterness
i.e. they put a curse on everyone
i.e. they are swift to shed blood, like the Gentiles, etc.
i.e. crushing
i.e. they cause misfortune to everyone; or the misfortune is their own
i.e. so that no one may boast that he has been saved by his own merit
i.e. in the bodies and souls of sinners
i.e. it is through Jesus Christ that everyone is justified.
i.e. a high thing that is not understood, i.e. it is above you.
i.e. through faith alone, i.e. through faith in Jesus Christ.
i.e. it is He who has ordained it, and it is He also who has redeemed it, i.e. through blood.
i.e. for it has been hidden in the mysteries of the Godhead, that He may be propitious to those who believe that they have been freed by His blood.
i.e. through the faith of everyone who believes in his salvation through blood.
i.e. there is nothing in it for you to boast of.
i.e. a question, i.e. through works of the law?
i.e. no, i.e. it is all the same: there would be no boasting.
i.e. it is through it that there is glorying.
i.e. did He create them alone? Did He not create all men? This is an answer to the mind of the Jews.
i.e. it is nearer to the Gentiles, i.e. because before the Law saints pleased God, such as Abel, Seth, Enoch, Noah.
i.e. though I should say it, the God of the Jews and the God of the Gentiles is one God, etc.
i.e. those who believe without historical (literal) circumcision.
Do we destroy it? i.e. when we say 'through faith'.
i.e. we do not destroy it.
i.e. while we prove that what He promised is true, as 'I will give you a heart of flesh', i.e. instead of a stony one, so that it may be spiritual circumcision; and not [?] destruction of the law.
i.e. according to the circumcision of the flesh; or: he is our father according to the flesh, because they were of the race of Abraham.
i.e. it is through faith that he has been justified, not through works of the law.
i.e. according to debt.
i.e. if it were a reward, it would not be grace but it would be a debt; it is through grace, then, that he has been sanctified, not through fulfilment of the law.
i.e. to him who believes.
i.e. his faith justifies him.
i.e. it is freely, not through works.
i.e. blessed (literally 'fair') is his life.
i.e. it does not abide [only], i.e. its half [?] with Abraham
i.e. it is well that Abraham was sanctified through faith; was it through it [circumcision], then, or not?
i.e. when he was in circumcision
i.e. when he was in uncircumcision. It is certain to us that it was not in circumcision that faith was reckoned to him
i.e. so that there might be something in his body that would signify the cutting off of vices from his soul
i.e. a recapitulation concerning the sign, i.e. he was circumcised when his faith had been justified
or through uncircumcision, i.e. through not cutting
i.e. it is of no profit to them that they undergo bodily circumcision only, unless they fulfil the spiritual circumcision of vices
but he is the father of those who possess the perfection of faith, as Abraham had it
i.e. it was promised, then, that his offspring would be exalted, as in 'in your seed' etc.
i.e. it is through his faith that every good thing came
i.e. the Jews are the sons of Abraham, i.e. if it is those who have fulfilled the law who are the heirs
faith, i.e. which Abraham had before the fulfilment of the law
i.e. what was promised to Abraham would be destroyed, i.e. 'I have made you a father' etc.
i.e. so that there would be no grace of forgiveness, and there would be no promise to him if it had been promised through the law, for it is vengeance, for it is vengeance unless it is fulfilled
i.e. there is no transgression of the law unless the law forbids
i.e. not to him who is of the law, i.e. since it is freely given, its promise will be true
i.e. if his faith is like the faith of Abraham

i.e. there are two inheritances that Abraham received, i.e. a bodily inheritance through circumcision, i.e. the land of promise, and it is this that Isaac received, and through that he is father of the whole nation; and a spiritual inheritance through faith, and through that he is father of many nations
Pelagius: not of the nation of Israel only but of all, i.e. the faithful of the world
i.e. conception for Sarah

i.e. it was against hope for him when He said to him that he would be the father of many nations, for the ways of women had ceased in Sarah and he himself was very old; but nevertheless he believed that it would come to pass
i.e. his faith was not weak, though what was said was contrary to nature
i.e. half-dead
i.e. this is its approximation [?], I think
i.e. he did not hesitate [?]
i.e. through unbelief
i.e. for his faith strengthened him to believe
i.e. this testimony in Genesis was not written for Abraham alone, but it was written for our perfecting
i.e. this is what is written
i.e. so that we may follow his ways in faith
i.e. it is to us
i.e. God: it is belief in his Godhead
i.e. what was reckoned to Abraham, i.e. righteousness through faith
i.e. from the standpoint of believers, so that he might confirm the righteousness of believers; i.e. it is clear to us through his resurrection that he is true God
i.e. we boast
i.e. although, then
i.e. all were ungodly, as [it is written]: 'there is none that does good', etc.
i.e. it is 'scarcely' that I say, and not 'not': for for a good man

i.e. he commends [?], i.e. that he has deserved it of us that he should be loved by us, i.e. since he dared what no other dared, i.e. so readily, lest it be an injury to him; for when something is given undeservedly, then love is most commended, so that they may recognize how they ought to conduct themselves

i.e. much more does he who gave himself for the ungodly not allow his own to perish [?]; i.e. since he has saved us here from our sins, so that we have been justified from them, far readier will he be to save us from the wrath to come
i.e. we boast
i.e. peace with God through faith in Christ, etc.
i.e. without warning and without perception
i.e. it was not recognized until the law came, for it held the human race under its dominion
i.e. although I say 'it was not imputed'
i.e. this is an answer to the thinking of heretics who say: if Adam's sin did not harm those who did not sin, then Christ's righteousness does not benefit those who do not believe
i.e. of innumerable [sins]
Judgement, i.e. through one sin, with Adam; grace from many sins, with Jesus, for men
i.e. it has abounded

i.e., when it (sin) had become full through its being revealed through the law, then afterwards came the grace of Jesus Christ, because the law [brought] no one to perfection, etc. It was not imputed before; it is manifest before everyone now [?].
i.e., it was unto death, of punishment [?] and of the body.
i.e., it will be unto life.
i.e., it is through him that grace and truth and eternal life are.
i.e., what need [is there]? [?]
i.e., so that it may be more abundant for us.
i.e., from the Jews and from the Gentiles [?].

i.e., according to the likeness of his death to the mortal body from which he separated in the passion: there is no return for him to that body, but he is in the spiritual body of the resurrection, without expectation of death or decay; so there will be no return for us either to the mortal body of sin. For just as the body consists of members, so sin consists of vices.
i.e., when we are under baptism, it is the likeness of his burial and of his death for us.
i.e., this is why it has been destroyed.
i.e., but let it be living.
i.e., once for all from sin, as Christ's flesh died once for all.
i.e., the body of Christ is everliving after the resurrection in the glory of the divinity.
i.e., consider.
i.e., that you are dead as regards sin, but that you are living in Jesus Christ.
i.e., that you are everliving in Jesus Christ, since you are his members, because he himself is living always.
i.e., as deadly instruments which bring death to you.
i.e., so that you should obey it.
i.e., so that this would be what was there, where he said before: 'we who are dead to sin, how shall we live again?'
i.e., do not offer your members in the battle on the devil's side.
i.e., it has been forgiven you through grace.
i.e., what need [is there]? [?]
i.e., to obedience.
i.e., whichever of the two it is to, whether to sin or to God, i.e., by obeying, you are his slaves in that case.
i.e., of punishment [?]; that is its end [?].
i.e. of the obedience
i.e. eternal life is its end
i.e. I give thanks to God that, though you were under sin, you are not now
i.e. whatever nation, then, this epistle was written to, it is shown to have been under the yoke, since he says 'servants' etc.
i.e. it is not compulsion that has driven you [?], but it is your own will
i.e. the grace of God, i.e. not through yourselves, but through God and through his grace
as if he had said: the teaching in which you are instructed is not from your own power etc.
i.e. to every kind of uncleanness
i.e. to every kind of iniquity
i.e. all your members
i.e. for your justification
i.e. this, then, in the end: as you have served sin, serve righteousness and be holy
i.e. what fruit
i.e. it is right for you, though it is shameful to you, that you confess it, for the end etc.
i.e. that will be your sanctification
or, reward; and that is not the same ... with ... [?] righteousness. Stipendium, then, is the name of the wage that is given to soldiers for their soldiering
i.e. through faith in Jesus, or in the life in which Jesus is after his resurrection
i.e. is this a matter of doubt to you?
i.e. this is the author's address to the people of the law [?], i.e. it is good to address the people who have knowledge
i.e. whether long or short
i.e. it is to this that I compare it
i.e. her lawful husband
i.e. to an unlawful man
i.e. so that she would be an adulteress
i.e. though she be
i.e. of serving [?], i.e. by dying together (with him)
i.e. it is not adultery for you
i.e. he now applies this to themselves
i.e. those were the instruments for working sin at that time
i.e. in newness, since the sin which we served until now does not survive; it is that which brought death to us
i.e. in newness of life after the confession of faith, without sin
i.e. not in the old way, for that was under sin
i.e. though [?] ..., he puts it first
i.e. the sin, not [?]
i.e. that it would be sin
i.e. it is for this reason that it is called 'the law of sin', because it shows sins. He speaks in the person of one living under the law. Pelagius says: 'I did not perceive that it was sin.'
i.e. it is now that I have known that desire is sin, since it has been forbidden
i.e. through the commandment, i.e. its prohibition became an occasion of action for sin
i.e. the commandment was transgressed by it
i.e. it is the sin that has wrought all desire, i.e. the desire which the law forbade, sin has wrought it in me, and the commandment of the law was transgressed by it
i.e. I thought that sin was dead, since I did not perceive it
i.e. I thought that I was alive when I did not perceive sin, until the law came
i.e. it would have been life to me if I had fulfilled it
i.e. it brought death to me through transgressing it
i.e. what I do after its prohibition, i.e. 'you shall not covet'
i.e. this is a judgement and an answer to what was said: 'What then shall we say?' etc.
A question, i.e. [?]
i.e. is it that which causes death to me, that excellent commandment?
i.e. it is not the commandment that causes death to me
i.e. it is greater after it has been perceived than before
i.e. it is honouring the law that is done in the transgression
i.e. since Adam went against the will [of God]. Pelagius: I have become accustomed to live carnally
i.e. from Adam; or: my carnal will has sold me, so that I am under the yoke of sin
i.e. through the will of my flesh
i.e. it is that, although I do it
i.e. it is not in the flesh that it dwells, but it is the desire
i.e. it is not a permanent dwelling, but a portion of [temporary] lodging [?]
i.e. this is what 'perficere' means for him: the completion of the good thought without the addition of evil thought
i.e. the work of transgression, and not its completion, but it is a portion of thought
the deed: to accomplish it in the flesh
i.e. it is a portion of finding; however, it does not take the mastery
i.e. so that I [?] it
i.e. it is clear here, then, that it is a good law that he speaks of finding above
i.e. it is the soul that is ready to fulfil the law of God, not the body
i.e. ready to do evil
i.e. a desire in my mind for good thought, but carnal concupiscence does not allow it
i.e. [?] as if he had said 'in his law', i.e. in the law of servitude to sin
i.e. it is that which takes the mastery in my members
i.e. if the grace of God did not help me, it would do it nonetheless
i.e. here or yonder
i.e. they are those who believe in Jesus
i.e. the spiritual law, i.e. which gives life to us through faith in Jesus Christ
i.e. the law of the spirit has freed me from the law of sin
i.e. [the law of] Moses; it is through it that sin was shown, through which there is death
i.e. by the [?] of that justification
i.e. in the likeness of the flesh in which there was sin
i.e. in the acknowledgment of the suffering of his flesh
i.e. every justification that has been brought about in the Law
i.e. so that it might be fulfilled in us
i.e. it is in that way that we are holy
i.e. for it is not easy for them to be holy
i.e. these, however, are the ones who will be saved
i.e. to return evil for evil; this, then, is the prudence of the flesh: to think about every care of the world without thinking about heavenly things
i.e. it will be life
i.e. it will be peace with God
i.e. it is hateful to God
i.e. there is care upon it, however, i.e. thinking about worldly things
i.e. after the manner of every good teacher, he praises and soothes before he rebukes
i.e. it is [?] for you; your life is not servile
i.e. that, then, is how you are in the spirit, and it is easy for you to do good
i.e. so that you may not commit sin

i.e. though Christ is in you through the confession of faith in baptism, and the soul is alive through that, the body, however, is dead through the old sins, even though they have been cleansed through baptism; it is not capable of good works until the Holy Spirit awakens it
i.e. for that guest-house of the Spirit would not be servile
i.e. it is not sins of the flesh that are healed there now, though they were so before
i.e. that we should do the works of the flesh as we did before
i.e. though there is freedom, debts are owed by you and by all of us whom he has joined to them [?], for it is [?] of him to pay the debts
i.e. the death of punishment, i.e. or when the flesh dies
i.e. its killing, then, will not be a cause of sorrow
i.e. eternal life, i.e. it will be like this: it will be life if the deeds of the flesh are put to death
i.e. so that they are moved [?], i.e. if it is a driving [?], as is said of the Son: he was led by the Spirit
i.e. this, then, is the testimony that we are
i.e. that we may share his inheritance with Christ
i.e. 'we shall be like him', i.e. this is how we shall be co-heirs: if we suffer as Christ did, or with Christ, or with one another
i.e. the glory that was given to Christ, so that it may be given to us with him, as we know that when he appears we shall be like him
i.e. it is in expectation
i.e. unless it were of necessity
i.e. to serve the sons of God
i.e. we lament
i.e. for hope is in things unseen
i.e. for what the eye sees is not hoped for
i.e. patience is necessary for them

It is in this, then, that the Spirit helps our weakness: when we have one desire, i.e. the body and the soul and the spirit. This, then, is a fitting prayer, but we are not able to do it unless the Spirit inspires it. This, then, is how our prayer is weak: if it is present things that we pray for, the Spirit does not help us in that. This, then, is what the Spirit helps: when we pray for glory for our body and for our soul after the resurrection.
i.e. the Holy Spirit makes the intercession; it is he who is knowing
which cannot be told, i.e. which cannot be described, but by a hidden compunction of the heart
i.e. he calls the desire 'the Spirit's' because he inspires the desire in the person
i.e. what is good with God to pray for, that is what he inspires in his saints
whatever we do for the love of God, i.e. in prosperity and in adversity
i.e. there will be glory after it
i.e. these
i.e. foreordained
Pelagius: firstborn from the dead and in glory; he is the firstborn of the faithful in the resurrection and in the receiving of glory
i.e. it is his own beloved that he gave; great is the good to us
i.e. since he is on our side, whatever anything can do to us, it is clear that it is for us, not against us
i.e. it will not be precious to him as against us

i.e. it is not for one man or two that he suffered, but for all. Although Judas and the Jews were the ones who betrayed him, he would not have been betrayed unless the heavenly Father had delivered him up.
i.e. is this likely of him? It is not likely, for he is the one 'who justifies'; that is more likely of him than to condemn.
i.e. who will condemn? Understand: God.
i.e. in Jesus Christ, i.e. could he at the same time be redeeming us and condemning us? No, it could not be; that is not what his love for us would want.
i.e. I think that is nearer the truth than that he would condemn us, i.e. that is for our justification, not for our condemnation.
i.e. he has taken his seat.
i.e. he intercedes, i.e. the humanity that he took from us makes petition for us to the Godhead, so that we may not perish.
i.e. as he has tested us.
i.e. every day we are ready to go to martyrdom.
i.e. we have been reckoned.
i.e. anyone is free to slay us. Pelagius: it is not lawful for us to defend ourselves.
i.e. things present, the things promised to us; i.e. an angel would sooner lie than I would be separated, i.e. the one is more likely than the other.
i.e. the rank that is lower than the angels.
Venerable is the weapon in which I say it, for I am a member of Christ.
i.e. my conscience does not deceive me, for it is by the Holy Spirit that I vouch for it.
i.e. it is grievous to me that you are without faith.
i.e. it is from this that it is clear that I love you: 'for I wished', etc.
i.e. a captive.
i.e. of the Israelites, i.e. God chose them as sons for himself, as it says: 'Israel is my firstborn.'
i.e. they are the fathers of the men who are there now.
i.e. this is what we make light of: that Christ is from them.
i.e. he is the one who is chief over all things.
i.e. he is God, blessed for ever.
i.e. not all of them are Israelites.
i.e. those who have descended from the seed of Abraham are not all sons of the promise.
i.e., it is from Isaac that the chosen seed will be begotten, not from Ishmael.
i.e., like Ishmael and the unbelieving Israelites, i.e., they would not take the inheritance, because they are not children of the promise.
i.e., they are reckoned.
i.e., it is this.
i.e., at the end of a period of time.
i.e., it is from one seed that her two sons were born.
propositum, i.e., the predestination by which God predestined the choosing of the one through mercy, and the damnation of the other through due judgment.
i.e., he who is the elder, i.e., Esau.
i.e., through due judgment, for both of them would have deserved hatred if mercy had not come; i.e., it was not by nature that he hated him.
i.e., since he chose the one man without merit and hated the other, is it likely that that would be unjust of God?
i.e., no, it is not unjust.
i.e., [?] my judgment.
i.e., for he will have mercy on whoever is pleasing to him.
i.e., a person's desire does not profit anyone unless God gives [help] to his desire; similarly neque currentis: the one on whom God has mercy, it is to him that it is of profit.
i.e., it was to bring vengeance on him, not God's mercy.
i.e., through bringing vengeance on him.

i.e., in the person of those who used to say: the sin belongs to no one, it does not deserve punishment, since it is not easy to go against the will of God, i.e., since it is 'on whom he wills' etc.; so it does not depend on us.
i.e., who are you who argue back? i.e., even though you were to be engaged in interpreting his judgment concerning God [?].
i.e., the thing formed.
i.e., to the one who formed it.
i.e., it is not good, what you have made me.
i.e., does he not have power?
of the potter
of the clay

i.e. it is carefully that he made the one vessel
i.e. it is less carefully that he makes the other
though he be desirous
i.e. he has endured, i.e. he did not immediately inflict vengeance on them, though they had deserved it
i.e. fit for vengeance to be inflicted on them
i.e. it was not for their good that they were spared, but so that the glorification of his saints might be all the more timely to him
i.e. those for whom he has prepared mercy
i.e. to be saved, though they did not deserve it

i.e. it will not be only those of the Jews who will be chosen who will be in that glory; believing Gentiles too will be there. Your own brother Hosea prophesied the reception of the Jews and the choosing of the Gentiles
i.e. what was not one's own will be made one's own there, i.e. my not-people will be a people to me
i.e. in the place, i.e. of scripture; or 'he will be called'; or: it will not be your [former] name that will be upon you, i.e. 'people of God'
i.e. Gentiles who were not the people of God until now will be sons of God; that is their name now. That is indeed not a worse name
i.e. this is an address to the Gentiles, i.e. he prophesied to Israel that a few people of them would believe, though they be many
i.e. though they be many, few of them will believe
i.e. there will be some portion of them that will be saved, though not all; for he will bring the word that perfects man in the righteousness of good works
i.e. the number that will believe in him will be in righteousness
i.e. he prophesied it before it came to pass
i.e. we would have died and none of us would have survived
i.e. the Gentiles did not deserve their justification; he sets forth, then, the Law and its righteousness below
i.e. not the righteousness of the Law
i.e. they think the works of the Law sufficient for their justification
they have struck many blows against it
i.e. 'stone of stumbling' is a name for Christ
i.e. in the [?] it is the custom, then, regarding the stone against which many blows are struck: he who falls on it breaks his bones, but he on whom it falls dies; so is Christ the cornerstone
i.e. he does not conceal, then, that it is Christ who is the stone he has spoken of
i.e. he says this for this reason: so that you may not think that he did not love the Jews and did not desire their salvation.
i.e. it is my prayer to God.
i.e. that God may save them.
i.e. it was fitting to pray for them; their perishing would be a pity.
i.e. everyone who will believe in Christ will be righteous.
i.e. he will not be guilty; recto [?].
i.e. he says what the righteousness from faith is.
i.e. to seek another testament.
i.e. proprium Pauli, i.e. Paul gives a gloss on the testimony of the Old Testament.
i.e. it is not necessary; he has come already.
i.e. it is not necessary to raise him up; he has risen from the dead already. It is enough for us, then, to believe in the incarnation and the resurrection.
i.e. if 'quis ascendit', i.e. if you have said it [?].
i.e. Christ is here with his Gospel.
i.e. to the Gentiles, after its coming.
i.e. it is for this reason that it is 'prope' (near).
i.e. faith in the heart makes a person righteous.
i.e. confession in the mouth makes a person saved. Through these two things a person is saved and righteous, so that he will be both saved and righteous.
i.e. he says this in the person of the Jew: to him it is a wonder that there should be faith for the Gentiles, since prophets did not prophesy to them.
i.e. the preacher.
i.e. it has not come to them at all.
i.e. it is of those preachers that it was said.

i.e. in their view a special mark is necessary on the shoes of those who preach peace and who arrange peace among kings, for which it is said, 'it is to bring peace that they come'. This verse: that is a sign that there should be a special mark on the deeds of the preachers.
i.e. of those who preach the divine mysteries.
i.e. not many have believed what they have heard from us from you, O God, although we have preached to everyone. Alternatively: [not many have believed] what everyone has heard from us.
i.e. is it not a lie of yours, O Jews, what you say, that the Gentiles have not heard the prophecy of Christ? Not so: they have heard it.
i.e. unless one conceals it [?]
Pelagius: that the Gentiles were to be called to the faith; i.e. what I say is the more [?] for you: even Israel knew of the believing of the Gentiles.
i.e. your own leader says it at the beginning.
i.e. [you] Jews.
to jealousy, i.e. it will be a jealousy to you that the Gentiles should be in the faith; or, to imitation, i.e. you will imitate them in the receiving of the faith.
i.e. a non-nation, i.e. which was not a nation to me until now, before it believed.
i.e. he dared to say something, because he does not fear the people of the Jews.
i.e. he says this for the correction of the Israelites, so that they may not boast, even though it was foretold to them.
i.e. that is your name.
i.e. it is clear from the fact that he has not cast me out, and yet I am indeed an Israelite.
i.e. that is the origin of my race.
i.e. whoever of them would believe.
i.e. have you not heard, O Gentiles, in the Book of Kings, where it is written about Elijah?
i.e. to bring vengeance upon them.
Here he accuses his people before God.
i.e. they have destroyed, or they have dug down [the altars], and have practised the worship of idols there.
i.e. there is no one here worshipping you except me alone.
i.e. though I am but alone, [they seek] this, that I may not remain among them [?].
i.e. to worship me.
i.e. it is not you alone, though you say [so].
i.e. to worship Baal.
i.e. if it is of grace, works have not gone before it.
i.e. you say: why is it said to you? [?]
i.e. if works had gone before it; but [then it would be] a debt.
i.e. the one whom God has chosen through grace, not through the works of the law, as [he chose] the Gentiles.
i.e. the Jews, i.e. they did not attain righteousness through grace.
i.e. of the inner man, i.e. their understanding was left to its own will, and it was not for good that he brought them [to it].
i.e. the sins of Paul [?], or the sins of death.
i.e. he does not conceal whatever may come of it.
i.e. the altar on which offering is made to idols.
i.e. the idolatry.
i.e. vengeance.
i.e. the bending of it.
i.e. that it should be a fall without rising that would be there; God forbid, it is not so great as that.
i.e. is this the extent to which they have stumbled, that they should all depart from the faith of Christ? No; this, then, is a strengthening of the Jews in his view.
i.e. it is for this reason that God has chosen the Gentiles: because the Jews did not want faith, but chose their unbelief.
i.e. of the Gentile people.
i.e. it is they who are the 'world' above.
i.e. if they had all [believed], they would not be apostles only.
i.e. because it is to you that I preach.
i.e. it is I who am the apostle of the Gentiles.
i.e. in whatever way I may do it.
i.e. my kindred according to the flesh.
i.e. through that imitation, i.e. that they might be jealous of my being in the faith, and to see whether they would imitate [me].
i.e. it is a sufficient [?] salvation, the few of them who have believed.
or 'life', i.e. life in the faith, from the dead, i.e. [from being] in sin before.
i.e. the choice portion, i.e. Christ, or the apostle.
i.e. the whole people.
i.e. the ones joined [grafted] in.
i.e. the fruitful olive tree.
i.e. O Gentiles, i.e. do not rejoice that they have been broken off into perdition, because it is in their place [?] that you are.
i.e. it is clear to you that it is not you who supports it, but it is it that supports you.
i.e. he takes on the person of a Gentile: it is likely that you will say, 'It is for this reason that the branches were broken off, [?] so that I might go [?] in their place.'
i.e. so that I might be grafted in.
i.e. not for that reason, i.e. I would rather it had been theirs.

i.e. because you have been grafted in freely and not according to merit, i.e. this is my advice to you, O Gentile: do not be boastful, do not puff yourself up too greatly, and be steadfast in the faith.
i.e. so that you may not be driven away from the truth through pride, like the original branch.
i.e. these are the Jews who have separated from the faith of the patriarchs.
i.e. is it not likely? Or: lest it happen that he does not spare you, when in fact it is that he should spare you.
i.e. it is thus that there will be goodness for you.
i.e. his attitude towards him is better.
i.e. what you are in will not be secure for you unless you conduct yourself well.
i.e. what they were cut off from, however, will be natural to them.
i.e. for God is able.
i.e. after they have been cut off.
i.e. he is making a comparison here, then, for it was their custom to cut a tree and graft another tree into it.
i.e. it would be more fitting for them to be in it.
i.e. they thought they would be in it.
[?] ... [?] ... might be ... [?] ... it would be in their [?].

i.e. it is a portion of them that has not believed, and even they will believe. Otherwise: blindness, i.e. stupidity; 'in part', i.e. it happened for a short time 'in part', i.e. only for a time, as Pelagius says.
i.e. until all the Gentiles come in, or a portion of every nation.
i.e. Israel will be saved.
i.e. help will come to them, though late; but it will be good forever when it comes.
i.e. Gentiles; these men do not love me because I preach the Gospel to the Gentiles.
i.e. but they are dear to me, i.e. I love them; they are a chosen race to God.
i.e. forgiveness of sin
i.e. that he would not be false [?] in what he promised
i.e. there was a time when you did not believe, until the mercy of God came to you
i.e. they have deserved it, and they crucified Christ
i.e. it will be mercy, then, that will save them; it will not be merit or the work of the law, when they believe

He has concluded [Pelagius]. He found all in unbelief [Pelagius]; not by force but by reason, i.e. so that he might shut them in, i.e. so that there is no room for anyone there to boast of his own merits, so that the mercy of God may save them
i.e. this is the depth of this mystery: the salvation of the world and of all men through mercy, after they had all been deserving of death
i.e. no one knows them

Question: what are the riches here, and of wisdom and of knowledge, and what are the inscrutable judgements, and what are the unsearchable ways, and what is the mind of the Lord? Not hard: it is to this that all these things refer, to the disposition, which he has set forth, that was in the mysteries of the Godhead in the creating of the elements in the beginning. We do not think it easy, indeed, to leap from the morals and from the teaching of the people, which he has set forth, to the creation of the elements. It is evident that it follows on the discourse that went before, and this is what he marvels at here: the depth of the knowledge, in that God saved the human race through mercy.
i.e. it is not unfitting [?] for me to beseech you by mercy; it is through it that you have been saved
i.e. chaste and alien from sin, i.e. from all vices, for the soul is ready for the will of God; then the soul is roused to do good
i.e. as was offered under the Law before the door of the Temple: without any blemish of colour, without blemish of sin
i.e. every prayer that you make according to the will of God will be reasonable
i.e. renew your mind, i.e. let your understanding be wise, not as it was before

i.e. this, then, is the will of God, i.e. these three things, i.e. good and pleasing and perfect; and these are the same as the three things he spoke of before, i.e. a living and holy and pleasing sacrifice, etc.

i.e. this is 'to be wise beyond what is fitting' according to him: doing the thing he has forbidden. This, however, is 'to be wise unto sobriety': not doing anything he has forbidden, and fulfilling what he has commanded.
i.e. as he gives it to each according to his faith
i.e. For sight cannot come about except in the eyes, etc. i.e. one work, however, all the members sustain, i.e. one movement
i.e. we are a body to Christ, and he is head to us
i.e. are, i.e. each one separately
i.e. is, i.e. each is a member to the other
i.e. this is what causes that mutual help: because the gift of each is different
i.e. according as each one's share of grace has come from God
i.e. the gift of each is different
i.e. let it be according to the rule of faith, i.e. not like the false prophets who used to prophesy beyond the faith
i.e. let it be ministering, i.e. in obedience to everyone

i.e. let him who teaches be [so], i.e. 'let each one [remain] in that in which he was called', etc.; or, teaching to everyone, i.e. to people after baptism, i.e. let it be in teaching, i.e. fulfilling it, so that it may be an example to everyone
i.e. strengthening everyone
i.e. let it be in simplicity
i.e. let it be in cheerfulness, i.e. for God loves a cheerful giver
i.e. without pretence, i.e. let what is said in the mouth not be different from what is in the heart
i.e. let each be warm [?] towards the other out of brotherly love
i.e. let each give honour to another and not give it to himself
i.e. not slothful
i.e. that the ardour of the love of the Spirit may be in us
i.e. let it be God whom we serve
i.e. be strengthened in expectation of future glory
i.e. let it be patient
i.e. let us be steadfast in prayer, so that tribulation can be endured
i.e. blessing is not enough if you curse; nor, again, is not cursing enough unless you bless
i.e. let everyone's joy be joy to you
i.e. let everyone's sorrow be sorrow to you
i.e. that joy or that sorrow, as if it had happened to you
i.e. every humble deed, let that be what you do
i.e. evil in return for evil
i.e. for that is the true prudence
i.e. whatever good there may be, let that be what you do
i.e. 'that they may see your works', etc., i.e. good deeds towards them
i.e. if it be in your power
i.e. however it may be, let there be peace on your part towards everyone, even though you are being persecuted
i.e. let it not be by force that you [?], lest anger take hold of you, or if anyone strikes you, etc.
i.e. your vengeance, i.e. it will be fitting for your benefit; you will have its reward.
i.e. it is likely that it is true.
i.e. perhaps it is more fitting for you that your vengeance should come from me than that you should render vengeance yourselves.
i.e. do not make yourself equal with him in evil, so that you may not both be evil.
i.e. Pelagius: he is said to have conquered who has drawn the other over to his own side, i.e. do good to him and he will be good afterwards.
i.e. to the power that protects; not [?] to power [?].
i.e. unless it be from God.
i.e. the powers: it is God who has ordained them; or, the powers that exist have been ordained by God.
i.e. since God has ordained them, what then of coming against them [?]
i.e. they will have the reward of their resistance; it is to their own condemnation; no one [?] good to them [?].
i.e. vengeance, i.e. they obtain it.
i.e. good work does not fear them, i.e. fear of them.
i.e. it would be more fitting for evil-doing [to fear them], since what he does is magnify good deeds and destroy evil deeds.
It has been declared, then, which powers it is right to serve, i.e. those who punish evils and magnify good things.
i.e. in the desire.

i.e. you will have benefit as a reward for good deeds. Origen: i.e. you will receive praise from God if you are subject to kings for God's sake, i.e. it is he who gives you a reward in return for your good deed.
i.e. thus it is fitting for you to fear him.
i.e. it is fitting to fear him, for it is to inflict vengeance that he bears that sword.
i.e. it is not [?] on his part, for it is by the grace of God that he inflicts vengeance on you.
i.e. not for one another.
i.e. since he punishes every evil and magnifies every good.
since he is able to inflict vengeance on you.
i.e. since you know that he is engaged in good, i.e. since he is a minister of God.
i.e. it is so.
i.e. give them what is due to them
i.e. it is right to give it to them
i.e. do not be neglectful about it
i.e. dues
i.e. let nothing be owed by you, i.e. lay aside all debts, so that you may be free for love
i.e. except this
i.e. in this saying
i.e. it is the time for doing good, or of the New Testament, or for fulfilling it rightly, the love of one's neighbour
i.e. of battle
i.e. whether it is to service or to suffering that one goes
i.e. as in the daytime our walking should be seemly, because it is by day that we walk about and see our way
... i.e. in sharing beds (lit. co-lyings) i.e.
i.e. every kind of contention
i.e. in jealousy, i.e. in envy
i.e. be a garment for the Lord, so that he may dwell in you; or, let Christ be a garment for you
i.e. let it not be according to the will of your flesh that you are
i.e. let it not be in order to judge him
i.e. let it not be in disputes, i.e. let it not be your thought that what he is is not good
i.e. it is to them that 'take up' is said
i.e. his faith is strong; every food is safe in his view
i.e. he whose faith is weak
i.e. he eats only bread; that is better in his view, as was the case with Daniel and the three youths
i.e. let him not show contempt for him
i.e. because he has been called by grace. Pelagius: He has called him just as he has called you, i.e. his worth is no less to Him than yours
i.e. what kind of person are you (lit. has it fallen to you to be)?
That is, he is not your servant; he is God's servant.
That is, there will be a time when he will not be weak.
That is, he keeps a special day.
That is, they keep no special day, but for them it is always a time of abstinence.
That is, let each person do what seems good to him, if it is for God.
That is, the one who fasts.
That is, none of us belongs to another; we all belong to God. It is not wrong for him to have us as his own, whether we live or die. That is why he suffered, etc.
That is, so that we may all be his.
That is, the thing over which you [?] is not yours, and the person you judge is not yours.
That is, perhaps he is a good man even though he does not eat every food.
That is, perhaps he is good even though he eats his food.
That is, there is a judge there besides you, namely God. It is he who knows the matter there, not as you do.
That is, he has foretold that day of judgement.
That is, everyone will make their confessions on that day.
That is, each person will give an account for himself.
That is, leave judgement to God, that is, a judgement that is [?] … Do not make one, except 'that you do not put,' etc.
That is, that judgement will be left to you.
That is, let it be you who give way to the [?] … your righteousness [?], who is weak, 'for everything that is not of faith' [?] … That is, do not force on anyone something he does not want.
That is, a denial [?]: making him eat what he does not want.
That is, it is in him that I trust.
That is, but it is unclean to him.
That is, it is unclean.
That is, if you do not give way to his weakness.
That is, give up the sweet foods and eat the foods your own people eat here, so that he is not the one who has to give way to you.
That is, Christ suffered more for him, namely death. Since that is so, give up the foods you love.
i.e. it is not that it brings you into [?], though you are one who eats [everything].
i.e. this, however, is the kingdom.
i.e. siding with the person who does not eat every food.
i.e. not siding with him.
i.e. which offends him.
i.e. he denies it.
i.e. it is out of weakness that he abstains.
i.e. we know that it is perfection of faith that you have in whatever you do.
i.e. it is not anyone [?] who sees it, but faith.
i.e. let it go with himself [?], i.e. let him not bring it against anyone.
i.e. no one should show contempt for anyone's weakness because of his own perfection.
i.e. who judges himself because of the weakness of his faith, i.e. because of its imperfection.
i.e. he is guilty.
i.e. we who are strong.
i.e. their weaknesses.
i.e. siding with them.
i.e. that is what is good for you.
i.e. love of one's neighbour is the building up of charity.
Pelagius: What he suffered did not please him, but it profited us. I.e. it is no harder for you than for Christ, for he suffered great pain in obedience to the Father.
i.e. but it is as was written, i.e. in Isaiah.
i.e. the reproaches.
i.e. Jesus says that.
i.e. for there would have been no need to write them if it were not to strengthen us in tribulations.
i.e. so that each may love the other.
i.e. according to the commandment of Jesus, or as Jesus Christ did for us.
i.e. one mind among you about it, and one deed, i.e. a deed of charity.
i.e. let each receive the other through charity (per caritatem), i.e. doing good to him.
i.e. for it was through humility that that receiving took place.
i.e. to show that he is true God, and that it is he who was foretold to the patriarchs: that the Son would be worthy of worship even though the form of his race would be upon him.
i.e. let them worship God; good is the favour he has given them, i.e. mercy (misericordia).
i.e. it was foretold long ago that God would be worshipped among the Gentiles.
i.e. since it is not difficult for you.

i.e. of Christ according to the flesh. Or 'root' (radix), i.e. Christ, because he is the root of Jesse according to his divinity: he himself created Jesse. But according to the flesh, Jesse is his origin.
i.e. the power of the Holy Spirit, i.e. it is he who strengthens us so that we may persevere in that perfect hope.
i.e. you have gained knowledge (scientia).
i.e. each is able to teach another.
i.e. of teaching or of preaching (docendi or praedicandi), for I have received grace (gratiam) to preach to everyone.
i.e. except what Christ says through me (per me).
i.e. into their obedience.
i.e. Illyricum, i.e. a region between Italy and Greece, i.e. next to Greece on the west and next to Italy on the east.
i.e. but my own labour.
i.e. it is of me that it was foretold that the Gentiles would see through me (per me).
for that reason.
i.e. it is long since I have had the desire to come to you.
i.e. [?] a circuit to you; I will visit you on my way.
i.e. that I may be escorted into Spain.
Pelagius: that this was useful to them (hoc sibi utile esse), i.e. it is [?] to them.
i.e. they have undertaken to make a collection.
i.e. they are debtors, i.e. they ought to minister (ministrare).
i.e. when I have completed it.
i.e. to the lowly [?]
i.e. I know that she will not go about [?] with anyone among you.
i.e. that you may help me [?] by praying for me in your prayers.
Here it is shown that everyone ought to pray to God for one another.
i.e. it is clear that he had been hindered [?] from going into Judea.
i.e. that they may be thankful.
i.e. what I have obtained through the fruit of my preaching is carried to the saints who are in Jerusalem.
i.e. that we may have a sojourn with you, i.e. after labour.
i.e. as is fitting and as is worthy of the saints, i.e. it is worthy of the saints to receive anyone who comes to them; and indeed it is in the Lord himself.
i.e. as is worthy of the saints: a welcome to the saints, i.e. in the Lord.
i.e. whatever she may need, give it to her.
i.e. a sign of fair greeting and of peace always where a greeting is given, i.e. be at peace with them, and let a greeting be carried from you.
i.e. they laid down, i.e. in persecutions, i.e. they were ready to undergo martyrdom for my sake.
i.e. to Priscilla and Aquila.
i.e. those to whom I preached the faith.
i.e. household.
i.e. the household of Priscilla and Aquila.
i.e. first, i.e. in believing in Asia; or in Asia itself he gave his firstfruits to Christ in believing.

i.e. from the beginning, i.e. he is the first man of the people of Asia who first believed in Christ; or 'a principio', i.e. from leadership, i.e. he was one of the leaders of Asia who believed in Christ.
O Romans, i.e. in strengthening whatever had been preached to you.
i.e. by birth; or their apostleship is noble because they came to Christ [?], and because they were members of the household [?] like me; or helping the apostles.
i.e. be at peace with all of them, and take an example from their good deeds.
i.e. because he preaches well and fulfils the gospel.
i.e. in every tribulation.
i.e. proven in faith.
i.e. the household of Aristobulus; be at peace with them.
i.e. in fulfilling the Gospel.
i.e. their whole household, i.e. of Philologus and Julia.
i.e. they greet you, i.e. they bless you.
i.e. take heed.
i.e. that is not what you have read in the Gospel.
Pelagius: through flatteries and adulations composed in speech, i.e. the outward appearance of their teaching is beautiful, but its inner substance is poisonous.

Obedience, i.e. your obedience to good and to evil is well known, and for that reason they try to subject you to their teaching; or, your obedience to the faith and to the Gospel is well known, therefore I ask you.
i.e. because your fame is well known; or, he says this so as not to offend them by having said that they were obedient, that is, easily turned toward being led astray.
i.e. he will be defeated in battle, and you will rout him, when God gives his help [?].
i.e. that is what he is here now [?].
i.e. in preaching the Gospel.
i.e. he came to me recently; or, Paul was lodging with him.
